name: Breckenridge-Myers-Peet-Vafa Spinning Black Hole
description: The extreme charged black hole of five dimensions that Jason Breckenridge, Robert Myers, Amanda Peet, and Cumrun Vafa set spinning in 1996, with angular momenta of equal size and opposite sign in its two planes and a horizon that does not rotate. Spun past its bound it has no horizon and no singularity, and its closed timelike curves are in view from far away.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, or $x^0 = cv$ in the ingoing chart, with the Ricci tensor $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. The mass parameter $\mu$ and the spin parameter $j$ are the same in every chart, with Breckenridge, Myers, Peet, and Vafa's $\omega = j/\mu$.
history: Jason Breckenridge and Robert Myers of McGill, Amanda Peet of Princeton, and Cumrun Vafa of Harvard set an extreme charged black hole of five dimensions spinning and posted the solution on 13 February 1996, a month after Andrew Strominger and Vafa counted the states of the static one [breckenridge1997, strominger1996]. They started from Myers and Malcolm Perry's black hole turning in one plane, added a flat sixth dimension, and returned to five through boosts and the duality between heterotic and type II strings, holding every scalar field constant [breckenridge1997, myers1986]. The extreme hole has angular momenta of equal size and opposite sign in its two planes, $J_1 = -J_2$ [breckenridge1997]. Its entropy $S = 2\pi k_B\sqrt{Q_HQ_F^2/2 - J^2/\hbar^2}$, with $Q_F$ its electric charge, $Q_H$ the charge of its antisymmetric tensor field, and $J = |J_1|$, equals for large charges that of the spinning states of the D-branes [breckenridge1997]. They wrote, "We find it remarkable that the agreement is precise, including the crucial numerical factors" [breckenridge1997]. The spin is bounded, $J^2 \le \hbar^2Q_HQ_F^2/2$, and "in going beyond this limit, closed timelike curves develop" [breckenridge1997].¶Breckenridge, Myers, Peet, and Vafa noted that the hole does not solve the Einstein-Maxwell equations of five dimensions, since with spin its magnetic dipole field and its charge switch on the Chern-Simons term of string theory at low energy [breckenridge1997]. With David Lowe and Strominger they built in March 1996 a family of seven parameters, two independent spins among them, whose entropy from the horizon matched the count of the branes at and just above extremality [breckenridge1996]. Arkady Tseytlin gave the spinning hole with three unequal charges and found that conformal invariance of the string's sigma model and regularity at short distances require the two spins to be equal [tseytlin1996extreme]. Renata Kallosh, Arvind Rajaraman, and Wing Kai Wong solved its Killing spinor equations and found its supersymmetry restored in full next to the horizon [kallosh1997].¶Jerome Gauntlett, Myers, and Paul Townsend took the hole as a solution of minimal supergravity in five dimensions, whose bosonic part is Einstein-Maxwell theory with a Chern-Simons term of fixed coefficient, and wrote it with the harmonic function $H = 1 + \mu/r^2$ on flat space of four dimensions, $\mu$ fixing the mass and $j$ the spin [gauntlett1999, gauntlett2003]. A supersymmetric black hole has a Killing vector timelike everywhere outside its horizon, so it has no ergoregion and its horizon cannot rotate, and in four dimensions it then has no angular momentum [gauntlett1999]. In five the horizon of this hole stands still, its sections 3-spheres squashed along their Hopf circles with area $2\pi^2\sqrt{\mu^3 - j^2}$ [gauntlett1999]. The angular momentum is in the Maxwell field, with "a negative fraction of the total" behind the horizon [gauntlett1999]. Inside the horizon the Hopf circles turn timelike near the singularity, and a closed timelike curve passes through every point there [gauntlett1999]. Jutta Kunz and Francisco Navarro-Lérida found numerically that above the Chern-Simons coefficient of supergravity there are black holes whose horizons turn against their angular momentum, as Gauntlett, Myers, and Townsend suspected [gauntlett1999, kunz2006].¶Gary Gibbons and Carlos Herdeiro separated the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the hole's geodesics in 1999 and found a Killing tensor beside its five Killing vectors [gibbons1999susy]. Its closed timelike curves lie inside a surface where the Hopf circles are null; for $j^2 < \mu^3$ that surface is inside the horizon, and the global structure resembles the extreme Reissner-Nordström hole's [gibbons1999susy]. For $j^2 > \mu^3$ the surface lies outside where the horizon would be, which no causal geodesic reaches, so the spacetime is geodesically complete and free of singularities, its closed timelike curves in view from far away [gibbons1999susy]. They took it to be the first supersymmetric spacetime with trivial topology known to be "a naked, totally non-singular time machine" [gibbons1999susy]. Herdeiro lifted the hole in 2000 to D1-branes and D5-branes in ten dimensions with a wave along them, whose universal cover has no closed timelike curves, and found the bound on the spin to be the unitarity bound of the conformal field theory of the branes [herdeiro2000]. Lisa Dyson argued that the hole cannot be spun past the bound, since the waves that hold its spin stop on a shell outside the region of closed timelike curves [dyson2004].¶Gauntlett, Jan Gutowski, Christopher Hull, Stathis Pakis, and Harvey Reall classified every supersymmetric solution of the theory; the hole is among those with a flat base of four dimensions, as is a maximally supersymmetric analogue of Gödel's universe [gauntlett2003]. Reall proved that near its horizon a supersymmetric black hole of the theory looks locally like flat space, anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions times a 2-sphere, or this hole near its horizon, and in the last case is this hole if its supersymmetric Killing vector is timelike outside [reall2003]. Henriette Elvang, Roberto Emparan, David Mateos, and Reall found the second case in 2004, a supersymmetric black ring that shrinks to this hole at zero radius and whose spins differ at every radius above zero, so its charges differ from the hole's [elvang2004]. Gauntlett and Gutowski joined two such rings with the hole's charges and a total horizon area less than, equal to, or greater than the hole's [gauntlett2005]. Hari Kunduri and James Lucietti found a spherical black hole with the hole's charges and near horizon geometry and a sphere outside its horizon that cannot be shrunk to a point [kunduri2014]. Veronika Breunhölder and Lucietti found four kinds of black hole with the hole's charges, among them a black lens with horizon $L(3,1)$, and three can have more entropy than the hole near its bound on the spin [breunholder2019].¶Pieter-Jan De Smet found in 2005 that the hole's Weyl tensor is of Petrov type 22, less algebraically special than the type $\underline{22}$ of the static holes of five dimensions and of Myers and Perry's [desmet2005]. Davide Gaiotto, Strominger, and Xi Yin read the hole at the centre of a Taub-NUT space as a black hole of four dimensions with the same entropy, its spin there a D0-brane charge [gaiotto2006]. Ashoke Sen found the logarithmic corrections to the hole's entropy in agreement with the microscopic counts, down to their dependence on the number of gauge fields and on the spin [sen2012]. Alejandro Ruipérez derived in 2026 the hole with three unequal charges at first order in $\alpha'$, the square of the string length, and its entropy agrees with values found from a supersymmetric index [ruiperez2026].

related.text: The extreme hole of five dimensions with three charges and no spin. With $j = 0$ this hole is Strominger and Vafa's, the one whose states the D-branes counted first [breckenridge1997, strominger1996].
The vacuum hole turning in one plane, lifted to six dimensions and turned by boosts and dualities into this charged one. Breckenridge, Myers, Peet, and Vafa started from it [breckenridge1997].
The static hole of five dimensions. With $j = 0$ this hole is its extreme charged version, which Gauntlett, Myers, and Townsend note is sometimes called Tangherlini's [gauntlett1999].
The charged hole of four dimensions. With $j = 0$ this hole is the extreme Reissner-Nordström hole of five dimensions [gauntlett1999].

The charged spinning hole of four dimensions. With its mass equal to its charge it is singular unless it has no spin, and this hole of five dimensions is supersymmetric and regular with spin [gauntlett1999].

A rotating universe, homogeneous, with closed timelike curves through every point. Minimal supergravity of five dimensions, the theory of this hole, has a maximally supersymmetric analogue of it [gauntlett2003].
Inside its region of closed timelike curves, where the Hopf circles are timelike, this hole is similar to the outer reaches of Lorentzian Taub-NUT [gibbons1999susy].

The throat of the fastest spinning Kerr hole, a circle fibred over anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions. Next to its horizon this hole is homogeneous too, a squashed 3-sphere fibred over that space [gauntlett1999].

A black ring turning around a hole, in vacuum. In the supergravity of this hole concentric rings are supersymmetric, with or without a hole at their centre, and two of them can share its charges [gauntlett2005].
The vacuum of five dimensions on Taub-NUT. At the centre of a Taub-NUT space this hole is a black hole of four dimensions with the same entropy [gaiotto2006].

Supersymmetric solutions whose naked singularity turns back massive particles. Spun past its bound this hole turns back every causal geodesic with no singularity, which Gibbons and Herdeiro likened to a repulson [gibbons1999susy].

The throat of the extreme charged hole of four dimensions, anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a 2-sphere. Next to its horizon this hole with $j = 0$ is anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a round 3-sphere [gauntlett1999].

coordinates.name: Breckenridge-Myers-Peet-Vafa Radius, Hopf Angles
domains: r^6 = j^2 \;\text{(the velocity of light surface)}

parameters.description: Mass parameter, an area, with the mass $M = 3\pi c^2\mu/(4G)$

Spin parameter, a length cubed, with the angular momentum $J = -\pi c^3j/(2G)$ about the Killing vector $2\partial_\psi$ of the isotropic chart; the closed timelike curves lie behind the horizon for $j^2 < \mu^3$

coordinates.convention: We use Breckenridge, Myers, Peet, and Vafa's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, with $t$ a time, $r$ a length, and $\theta$, $\phi$, and $\psi$ the Hopf angles of the 3-sphere.

coordinates.convention: We use Gibbons and Herdeiro's coordinates $(t, r, \alpha, \beta, \gamma)$, with the radius $r$ of the Hopf chart and the Euler angles $\beta = 2\theta$, $\alpha = \psi + \phi$, and $\gamma = \psi - \phi$ of the 3-sphere.

coordinates.convention: We use Gauntlett, Myers, and Townsend's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, with $r$ the radius of flat space of four dimensions, $\sqrt{r^2 + \mu}$ the radius of the Hopf chart, and $\theta$, $\phi$, and $\psi$ the Euler angles $\beta$, $\alpha$, and $\gamma$ of Gibbons and Herdeiro.

coordinates.name: Ingoing, Euler Angles

parameters.description: Mass parameter, an area, with the mass $M = 3\pi c^2\mu/(4G)$

Spin parameter, a length cubed, with the angular momentum $J = -\pi c^3j/(2G)$ about the Killing vector $2\partial_\psi$ of the isotropic chart; the closed timelike curves lie behind the horizon for $j^2 < \mu^3$

coordinates.convention: We use Gauntlett, Myers, and Townsend's ingoing coordinates with the advanced time $v$, $c\,dv = c\,dt + \sqrt{1 - j^2/r^6}\,dr/(1 - \mu/r^2)^2$, the radius $r$ of the Hopf chart, the angles $\theta$ and $\phi$ of the isotropic chart, and $\tilde\psi$ with $d\tilde\psi = d\psi + 2j\,dr/\left((1 - \mu/r^2)r\sqrt{r^6 - j^2}\right)$.
geodesics: \ddot{v} + \dfrac{2\mu\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^2 - \mu\right)}{r^8}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{j\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)\cos\theta}{r^8}\dot{v}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{j\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)}{r^8}\dot{v}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}{4r^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^6 - 2j^2\sin^2\theta + 2j^2\right)}{4r^8}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)\cos\theta}{2r^8}\dot{\phi}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)}{4r^8}\dot{\tilde\psi}^2 = 0

\ddot{r} + \dfrac{2\mu\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^3}{r^9}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(2\mu\,r^4 - j^2\right)}{r^6\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)\cos\theta}{r^9}\dot{v}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)}{r^9}\dot{v}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{3j^2}{r\left(r^3 + j\right)\left(r^3 - j\right)}\dot{r}^2 + \dfrac{j\left(2r^6 - 3\mu\,r^4 + j^2\right)\cos\theta}{r^6\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{r}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{j\left(2r^6 - 3\mu\,r^4 + j^2\right)}{r^6\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{r}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2}{4r^3}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2\left(r^6 - 2j^2\sin^2\theta + 2j^2\right)}{4r^9}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)\cos\theta}{2r^9}\dot{\phi}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)}{4r^9}\dot{\tilde\psi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\tilde\psi} + \dfrac{4\mu\,j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)^2}{r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{v}^2 + \dfrac{4j\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)}{r\left(r^3 + j\right)\left(r^3 - j\right)}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{2j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\cot\theta}{r^6}\dot{v}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{2j^2\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)\cos\theta}{r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{v}\dot{\phi} - \dfrac{2j^2\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(r^2 - 2\mu\right)}{r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{v}\dot{\tilde\psi} + \dfrac{6j^2\cos\theta}{r\left(r^3 + j\right)\left(r^3 - j\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{2r^6 + 4j^2}{r\left(r^3 + j\right)\left(r^3 - j\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)}{2r^2\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^6 - j^2\sin^2\theta + j^2\right)\csc\theta}{r^6}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{\left(r^3 + j\right)\left(r^3 - j\right)\cot\theta}{r^6}\dot{\theta}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(r^6 - 2j^2\sin^2\theta + 2j^2\right)}{2r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)\cos\theta}{r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{\phi}\dot{\tilde\psi} - \dfrac{j\left(r^2 - \mu\right)\left(r^6 + 2j^2\right)}{2r^8\,\sqrt{r^3 + j}\sqrt{r^3 - j}}\dot{\tilde\psi}^2 = 0
